# Internal Petstore service.
#
# All endpoints require a bearer token except the health check. Rate limits
# apply to the search endpoints, so keep an eye on the X-RateLimit headers when
# running the whole folder.
# @auth basic {{user}} hunter2
@baseUrl = https://petstore.example.com
@user = alice
=== _postman-post.js ===
// Untranslated Postman test script for "Petstore API".
//
// Nothing runs this file. It is a plain ES module (docs/FORMAT.md §2.4), kept
// so the logic is not lost. To make it run, port what you need into a file
// named _post.js, or into a {% %} block in the request itself.
//
// The calls that usually matter:
//
//   postman.setEnvironmentVariable("id", v)  ->  vars.session.set("id", v)
//   pm.response.json()                       ->  response.json()
//   pm.test("name", fn)                      ->  test("name", fn)
//
// A script gets a JavaScript realm and nothing else: no fetch, no require, no
// filesystem, no timers (docs/FORMAT.md §9.3).

pm.test("fast", () => pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime).to.be.below(500));

=== pets/_postman-pre.js ===
// Untranslated Postman pre-request script for "Pets".
//
// Nothing runs this file. It is a plain ES module (docs/FORMAT.md §2.4), kept
// so the logic is not lost. To make it run, port what you need into a file
// named _pre.js, or into a {% %} block in the request itself.
//
// The calls that usually matter:
//
//   postman.setEnvironmentVariable("id", v)  ->  vars.session.set("id", v)
//   pm.response.json()                       ->  response.json()
//   pm.test("name", fn)                      ->  test("name", fn)
//
// A script gets a JavaScript realm and nothing else: no fetch, no require, no
// filesystem, no timers (docs/FORMAT.md §9.3).

pm.environment.set("requestId", pm.variables.replaceIn("{{$guid}}"));
=== pets/create-pet.http ===
# @name Create pet
POST {{baseUrl}}/v2/pets
X-Request-Id: {{$uuid}}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Rex",
  "tag": "dog",
  "createdAt": "{{$isoTimestamp}}"
}

=== pets/get-pet.postman-post.js ===
// Untranslated Postman test script for "Get pet".
//
// Nothing runs this file. It is a plain ES module (docs/FORMAT.md §2.4), kept
// so the logic is not lost. To make it run, port what you need into a file
// named get-pet.post.js, or into a {% %} block in the request itself.
//
// The calls that usually matter:
//
//   postman.setEnvironmentVariable("id", v)  ->  vars.session.set("id", v)
//   pm.response.json()                       ->  response.json()
//   pm.test("name", fn)                      ->  test("name", fn)
//
// A script gets a JavaScript realm and nothing else: no fetch, no require, no
// filesystem, no timers (docs/FORMAT.md §9.3).

pm.test("status is 200", function () {
    pm.response.to.have.status(200);
});
=== pets/list-pets.http ===
# @name List pets
# Returns pets, newest first.
GET {{baseUrl}}{{petsPath}}?limit=20&status=available
Accept: application/json

Rex at the beach

POST {{baseUrl}}/graphql
Content-Type: application/json

  "query": "query Search($q: String!) {\n  pets(query: $q) {\n    id\n    name\n  }\n}",
  "variables": {
    "q": "rex"
  }
}

=== REPORT ===
Imported "Petstore API": 13 requests, 3 folders, 1 environments, 24 files

Skipped (7)
  - _folder.http: secret variable "legacyToken": move it to an environment as {"$secret": "keychain"}
  - _folder.http: disabled variable "unused"
  - pets/list-pets.http: disabled query parameter "debug"
  - pets/list-pets.http: disabled header "X-Debug"
  - pets/update-pet-form.http: disabled form field "legacy"
  - health-check.http: auth type "oauth2" is not supported; configure it manually
  - env/petstore-dev.json: disabled variable "debug"

Needs attention (9)
  - _folder.http: basic password is a literal value in the collection; move it to an environment variable
  - _postman-post.js: test script for "Petstore API" imported as a module; nothing runs it until you port it to _post.js
  - pets/_postman-pre.js: pre-request script for "Pets" imported as a module; nothing runs it until you port it to _pre.js
  - pets/get-pet.postman-post.js: test script for "Get pet" imported as a module; nothing runs it until you port it to get-pet.post.js
  - pets/upload-photo.http: form file "photo" points at /Users/alice/Pictures/rex.jpg, a path on the exporting machine; copy the file into the collection and fix the path
  - infra-aws/s3-object-literal-keys.http: AWS secret key was a literal in the export; replaced with {{awsSecretKey}}. Set it as a keychain secret, or switch to '@auth aws profile=<name>' to use your local AWS credentials
  - infra-aws/s3-object-literal-keys.http: AWS session token was a literal in the export; replaced with {{awsSessionToken}}
  - env/petstore-dev.json: secret variables written as keychain references; their values were NOT imported and must be stored in the keychain: token, apiKey
  - pets/_postman-pre.js: Postman dynamic variable {{$guid}} has no Otis equivalent and will be reported as unresolved

Notes (7)
  - pets/create-pet.http: added Content-Type: application/json (Postman sets it implicitly)
  - pets/update-pet-form.http: added Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded (Postman sets it implicitly)
  - pets/upload-photo.http: added Content-Type: multipart/form-data (Postman sets it implicitly)
  - search/graphql-search.http: added Content-Type: application/json (Postman sets it implicitly)
  - search/search.http: API key appended to the URL as api_key=...
  - infra-aws/_folder.http: AWS auth uses explicit keys; consider '@auth aws profile=<name>' so no key material lives in the collection
  - infra-aws/s3-object-literal-keys.http: AWS auth uses explicit keys; consider '@auth aws profile=<name>' so no key material lives in the collection
